alertitem.name: Missing Anti-Missing X-Content-Type-Options header
alertitem.desc: The X-Content-Type-Options header was not set to 'nosniff'. This allows older browsers to perform MIME-type sniffing which can lead to security vulnerabilities.
alertitem.solution: Ensure that the application sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff' for all responses.

alertitem.name: Cross-Site Scripting (Reflected) in search query
alertitem.desc: The application reflects user input in the response without proper encoding, allowing an attacker to inject malicious scripts. The search parameter does not sanitize input before rendering it in the HTML response.
alertitem.solution: Encode all user-supplied data before rendering it in HTML. Use Content-Security-Policy headers to mitigate the impact.

alertitem.name: Potential SQL Injection in login form
alertitem.desc: The login form appears vulnerable to SQL injection. User-supplied input in the email parameter is concatenated directly into an SQL query without parameterization. An attacker could bypass authentication or extract sensitive data.
alertitem.solution: Use parameterized queries or ORM for all database operations. Never concatenate user input directly into SQL statements.

alertitem.name: Cookie missing SameSite attribute
alertitem.desc: The application sets cookies without the SameSite attribute, which may allow cross-site request forgery attacks in older browsers.
alertitem.solution: Set the SameSite attribute to 'Lax' or 'Strict' on all cookies.

alertitem.name: No minimum password length enforced
alertitem.desc: The registration form does not enforce a minimum password length or complexity requirements.
alertitem.solution: Implement password policy requiring minimum 8 characters with mixed case, numbers, and special characters.

alertitem.name: Server header leaks version information
alertitem.desc: The HTTP server header contains version information that could help an attacker identify vulnerable software.
alertitem.solution: Configure the web server to suppress or modify the Server response header.

alertitem.name: Content Security Policy header is missing
alertitem.desc: The Content-Security-Policy header is missing, which could allow XSS and data injection attacks.
alertitem.solution: Implement a Content-Security-Policy header to restrict resources the browser is allowed to load.

alertitem.name: OS command injection via file upload parameter
alertitem.desc: The file upload functionality passes user input to a system command without sanitization. An attacker could execute arbitrary operating system commands on the server.
alertitem.solution: Avoid using system commands with user input. Use language-native APIs instead of shell commands. If shell commands are necessary, validate and sanitize all inputs strictly.

alertitem.name: Unvalidated redirect in return URL parameter
alertitem.desc: The application redirects users to an external URL specified in the return_url parameter without validation, enabling phishing attacks.
alertitem.solution: Validate redirect URLs against a whitelist of allowed domains before redirecting.

alertitem.name: DOM XSS via innerHTML in product review
alertitem.desc: The product review page uses innerHTML to render user comments, allowing DOM-based cross-site script injection.
alertitem.solution: Use textContent instead of innerHTML for rendering user-generated content. Implement DOMPurify or similar sanitization.

alertitem.name: Session token not regenerated after login
alertitem.desc: The application does not regenerate the session token after successful authentication, making session fixation attacks possible.
alertitem.solution: Regenerate the session ID after successful authentication using session.invalidate() or equivalent.

alertitem.name: Server supports deprecated TLS 1.0 protocol
alertitem.desc: The server accepts TLS 1.0 connections which have known vulnerabilities including BEAST and POODLE.
alertitem.solution: Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1. Only allow TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.

alertitem.name: Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to wildcard
alertitem.desc: The application returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * which allows any origin to make cross-origin requests, potentially exposing sensitive data.
alertitem.solution: Restrict CORS to specific trusted origins instead of using a wildcard.

alertitem.name: Debug stack trace exposed in error response
alertitem.desc: The application exposes debug stack traces in error responses, revealing internal paths and code structure.
alertitem.solution: Disable debug mode in production. Use custom error pages that do not reveal internal details.

alertitem.name: Application uses modern JavaScript framework
alertitem.desc: The application was detected as using a modern JavaScript framework with client-side rendering.
